info.name: RecipeDB 2 API
info.description:
This is a comprehensive documentation for all the API Endpoints of RecipeDB2 for accessing over 118,000 recipes, nutritional data, and meal planning features.

The documentation features example usage (with optional and required parameters) as well as example responses. For achieving a valid response for any API endpoint, the user is required to undergo authorization through an API key, which can be obtained at your Profile dashboard at [Foodoscope](https://www.foodoscope.com/).

You may also use the frontend variant of the RecipeDB API Endpoint Playground at [Foodoscope](https://www.foodoscope.com/) if you wish to, or directly try the API endpoints in cURL (or your desired terminal). The following is an example:

```
curl -X GET "http://cosylab.iiitd.edu.in:6969/recipe2-api/recipe/recipeofday" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <yourAPIkey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

 ```

For a detailed look at all the API endpoints and their parameters, please refer to the GET and POST methods below.

```
Note: While page and limit/page_size parameters are dynamic and can go up to an unlimited range, it is not recommended to put an extremely large value for either of the parameters. You might receive an empty response or a false success message.
The default values for both parameters are the recommended values.

 ```

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):** The note above about `page` and `limit` going "up to an unlimited range" no longer holds. `limit` is now at most **10** on every endpoint except **Get Dropdown Values** (at most **100**). A larger value returns `400` on most endpoints; a few older ones quietly cap it to 10. Each endpoint's description says what happens for a `page` past the last page.

## Getting started in Postman

1. Get your API key from your Profile dashboard at [Foodoscope](https://www.foodoscope.com/).
2. Open this collection, go to the **Variables** tab and paste the key into the **Current value** of `apiKey`. Paste only the key: Postman sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <your key>` on every request.
3. `baseUrl` already points to the live server, `http://cosylab.iiitd.edu.in:6969`. If you run the backend on your own machine, change it to `http://localhost:3000`.
4. Open **Recipe of Day** (it takes no parameters) and click **Send**. If you get a recipe back, everything is set up.

### Common errors

| Status | Message | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `ApiKey is not provided` | The `apiKey` variable is empty. Do step 2. |
| `401` | `Invalid API key` | The key is wrong, or you typed `Bearer` in front of it (Postman already adds it). |
| `400` | any other message | A parameter is missing, unknown, repeated or out of range. The message names it. |
| `404` | e.g. `No recipes found...` | The request was valid but nothing matched, e.g. a misspelt region. |

## Valid values for text parameters

Most text parameters must match values stored in the database. Use **Get Dropdown Values** (`/recipe2-api/connections/dropdowns?type=...`) to list them; add `&search=...` to filter.

| Parameter | Used by | Where to get valid values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `region` | Recipe By Cuisine (`:region`), Recipe By Region Diet | `?type=region`, e.g. `Indian Subcontinent`, `Italian`, `Mexican`, `Middle Eastern`, `Southeast Asian`, `Chinese and Mongolian`, `Rest Africa`, `US`, `UK` |
| `continent` | Recipe By Cuisine | `?type=continent`, e.g. `Asian`, `European`, `African`, `Latin American`, `North American`, `Australasian` |
| `subRegion` (country) | Recipe By Cuisine | `?type=country`, e.g. `Indian`, `Chinese`, `Italian`, `Mexican`, `Lebanese`, `Moroccan` |
| `diet`, `diet_type` | Recipe By Recipe Diet, Recipe By Region Diet, Recipe Meal Plan | Fixed list: `vegan`, `pescetarian`, `ovo_vegetarian`, `lacto_vegetarian`, `ovo_lacto_vegetarian` |
| `:method` | Recipe By Recipes Method | `?type=process` |
| `utensils` | Recipe By Utensils | `?type=utensil` (separate several with commas) |
| `includeDietrxCategories`, `excludeDietrxCategories`, `excludeCategories` | Recipe By Category, Recipe By Recipe Day Category, Recipe With Ingredients Categories | `?type=category` |
| ingredient names | `includeIngredients`, `excludeIngredients`, `ingredient`, `exclude_ingredients` | `?type=ingredient&search=...` |
| `:flavor` | Recipe By Ingredients Flavor | FlavorDB category names such as `Fruit` or `Herbs and Spices` (no dropdown type for these yet) |

Region, country and continent names are not case-sensitive on Recipe By Cuisine.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** Photos on `images.media-allrecipes.com/userphotos/` no longer load (HTTP 403 for every file), so every endpoint sends `img_url: null` for those recipes (14,376 recipes, counted 4 Nov 2026). Recipe Micro Nutrition Info and Recipe By Recipes Method still leave out `url` and `img_url`, as they did before. An unknown path under `/recipe2-api` returns JSON `{ "success": false, "message": "Route not found" }` instead of an HTML page.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026), all endpoints:** A request containing a null character (`%00` in the URL, `�` in a JSON body) is a `400` "Null characters (%00) are not allowed in requests." (Links, Dropdowns and Flavor used to answer `500`). A POST body that is not valid JSON is a JSON `400` "Request body is not valid JSON." (it used to be an HTML error page).

> **Update (7 Nov 2026, later), all endpoints:** A path that does not exist, also outside `/recipe2-api`, is a JSON `404` "Route not found" (paths outside `/recipe2-api` used to get an HTML error page).

Page number.
**Default:** `1`
**Min Value:** `1`
**Max Value:** the last page (`totalPages`)

Must be a positive integer; otherwise `400`. A page beyond the last page also returns `400`.

Number of recipes to be shown per page.

**Default:** `10`
**Min Value:** `1`
**Max Value:** `10` (higher values return `400`)
Optional. Returns only the recipe with this id (`404` if it does not exist). `page` is ignored when this is given.

request.description:
Retrieves a paginated list of all available recipes in the database, optionally filtered by a single recipe id.

### Parameters

- **page** (Optional): positive integer, up to the last page (a page beyond it returns `400`). Ignored when `recipeId` is given
    
- **limit** (Optional): positive integer, max 10 (a higher value returns `400`)
    
- **recipeId** (Optional): string. Returns only that recipe (`404` if it does not exist)
    

Parameter names are case-insensitive and spaces around a name are ignored (`limit ` works like `limit`). Unknown or repeated parameters return `400`. An empty page/limit (`?page=`) uses its default.

request.description:
Returns the 'Recipe of the Day'. The recipe is picked from the date, so every request (and every server instance) returns the same recipe for a given UTC day, and it changes at the next UTC midnight. The response carries a `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<seconds until UTC midnight>` header, so clients can reuse it until then. Only recipes that have a photo of their own are picked (the generic placeholder image is never served). `meta.date` is the UTC day the recipe is for. The source `url` field is not included.

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - Takes no parameters. If no recipe can be picked the response is `404` "No recipe found".

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** This endpoint takes no query parameters; any parameter is a `400` (it used to be ignored).

query.description: Select ingredients to exclude.
Select categories to exclude.

request.description:
Generates a 'Recipe of the Day' while excluding specific ingredients or food categories.

### Parameters

- **excludeIngredients** (Optional): string
    
- **excludeCategories** (Optional): string
    

Both are comma-separated and case-insensitive. An unknown ingredient or category returns `400`. The first request of the day for a given filter picks the recipe; every later request with the same filter returns that same recipe (served from cache), and a filter with no match keeps returning `404` for the day. Like Recipe of the Day, recipes with a real photo are preferred; the response includes `img_url`, `url` and `meta.date` (the UTC day).

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):** Valid values: see **Get Dropdown Values** with `?type=category` and `?type=ingredient`, or the "Valid values" table in the collection overview.

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - Errors: `400` "Category not found: ..." or "Ingredient not found: ..." for a name that isn't in the database, `400` for any other query parameter, `404` "No matching recipe found today." when the filters exclude every recipe.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** Today's recipe is now chosen from **all** recipes that pass the exclusions (it used to look at 30 random recipes, so a strict filter could answer `404` for the whole day although matching recipes existed), and the choice comes from the date, so it stays the same all day, also after a server restart (it used to change on every restart). Recipes with their own photo still come first. A repeated request now has the same message as the first (it used to say "(cached)").

> **Update (9 Nov 2026):** In the first minute after a server restart (before the in-memory index is ready) the recipe is a random pick that is not cached; that pick now also comes from recipes with their own photo, so a strict filter no longer gets a recipe without a photo there.

request.description:
Provides macronutrient details (calories, fat, protein, carbohydrates) for recipes.

### Parameters

- **page** (Optional): positive integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): positive integer, max 10 (a higher value returns `400`)
    
- **recipeId** (Optional): string. Returns only that recipe's rows (`404` if it does not exist)
    

Parameter names are case-insensitive and spaces around a name are ignored (`limit ` works like `limit`). Unknown or repeated parameters return `400`. A page past the last page returns `200` with an empty `data` array.

> **Update (19 Oct 2026):**

request.description:
Provides detailed micronutrient data (vitamins, minerals, cholesterol) for recipes.

### Parameters

- **page** (Optional): positive integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): positive integer, max 10 (a higher value returns `400`)
    

Parameter names are case-insensitive and spaces around a name are ignored (`limit ` works like `limit`). Unknown or repeated parameters return `400`. A page past the last page returns `200` with an empty `data` array.

> **Update (19 Oct 2026):**
> - An empty or blank `page` or `limit` (e.g. `?page=&limit=` from a cleared form) now uses the default (`1` / `10`) instead of returning `400`.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** New optional `recipeId`: returns only that recipe's record (`404` if it does not exist, `400` if empty or longer than 32 characters), like Recipe Info and Nutrition Info.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** A `page` past the last one is now a `400` "Page N does not exist. Please provide a page between 1 and X." (it used to be an empty `200`), the same answer every list endpoint gives.

request.description:
Filters recipes based on preparation, cooking and total time ranges.

### Parameters

- **field** (Optional): string
    
- **min** (Optional): integer
    
- **max** (Optional): integer
    
- **page** (Optional): integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): positive integer, max 10 (a higher value returns `400`)

> **Update (19 Oct 2026):**
> - `min` and `max` are required: a missing or non-numeric value returns `400` ("Invalid range. Please provide valid min and max query parameters."). They cannot be negative: a negative value returns `400` (it used to return `200`).
> - An empty `field=` uses the default `total_time`. An empty or blank `page` or `limit` (e.g. `?page=&limit=` from a cleared form) now uses the default (`1` / `10`) instead of returning `400`.
> - Spaces around the `field` value are ignored (`field= total_time ` works).
> - Results are ordered by the selected time (lowest first), then by `_id`, so consecutive pages never repeat or skip a recipe.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** Each recipe now also has the core recipe fields: `Recipe_id`, `Recipe_title`, `Region`, `Sub_region`, `Continent`, `Calories`, `total_time`, `prep_time`, `cook_time`, `servings`, `img_url` (the same columns on every recipe list).

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** A `page` past the last one is now a `400` "Page N does not exist. Please provide a page between 1 and X." (it used to be an empty `200`), the same answer every list endpoint gives. `min` / `max` must be plain decimal numbers (`1e1`, `0x10` or a space are `400`; `.5` and `10.` work), and `page` / `limit` follow the same rules as the other list endpoints (`page=1e2` used to be read as page 1; `limit=1.5` is now a `400`). A parameter given twice is a `400`.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026, later):** When no recipe is in the range the answer is a `404` "No recipes found in the specified time range.", like the other list endpoints (it used to be a `200` with an empty list).

request.description:
Filters recipes based on primary flavor profiles or ingredient categories.

### Parameters

- **flavor** (Required): string. Case-insensitive "contains" match on the flavor category, matched as plain text (not a regular expression)
    
- **page** (Optional): positive integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): positive integer, max 10 (a higher value returns `400`)
    

Returns `404` when no ingredient matches the flavor. Parameter names are case-insensitive and spaces around a name are ignored (`limit ` works like `limit`). Unknown or repeated parameters return `400`. A page past the last page returns `200` with an empty `data` array.

> **Update (19 Oct 2026):**
> - Matching changed (18 Oct 2026): `flavor` now matches the whole category name plus its sub-categories, case-insensitive, instead of "contains". `Fruit` matches `Fruit` and `Fruit-...`, but no longer `Vegetable-Fruit`; a partial name such as `ui` returns `404`.
> - An empty or blank `page` or `limit` (e.g. `?page=&limit=` from a cleared form) now uses the default (`1` / `10`) instead of returning `400`.

**Update (Nov 2026):** `:flavor` is a FlavorDB category (Fruit, Herb, Dairy, Vegetable, Vegetable-Bulb, ...), not a taste word like `sweet`. An unknown value returns 404 and the message lists the valid values.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** A `page` past the last one is now a `400` "Page N does not exist. Please provide a page between 1 and X." (it used to be an empty `200`), the same answer every list endpoint gives.

request.description:
Nutrition of one ingredient **per 100 g** (USDA values; garlic gives 149 kcal).

Response: `data: { ingredient, ndb_id, per: "100 g", nutrition: { "Energy (kcal)": 149, "Protein (g)": 6.36, ... } }`.

Errors: missing `ingredient` or an unknown parameter → 400; no such ingredient → 404.

The older path `/recipe-nutri-ingredient/nutrition/:ingredient` returns the same response.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** The older path `/recipe-nutri-ingredient/nutrition/:ingredient` used to return one recipe's raw nutrition row (with `Recipe_id`, in that recipe's amount, plus a `cached` flag). It now returns the same per-100 g response as this request, so a client that read the old fields has to switch to `data.nutrition`.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** The older path form `GET /recipe2-api/recipe-nutri-ingredient/nutrition/:ingredient` (e.g. `/nutrition/garlic`) gives the same answer as `?ingredient=garlic`. It takes no query parameters; any is a `400`.

request.description:
Finds recipes that require specific kitchen utensils or equipment.

### Parameters

- **utensils** (Required): string. One name or a comma-separated list (`frypan,skillet` matches either). Case-insensitive "contains" match, matched as plain text (not a regular expression)
    
- **page** (Optional): positive integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): positive integer, max 10 (a higher value returns `400`)
    

Returns `404` when no recipe matches. Parameter names are case-insensitive and spaces around a name are ignored (`limit ` works like `limit`). Unknown or repeated parameters return `400`. A page past the last page returns `200` with an empty `data` array.

> **Update (19 Oct 2026):**
> - An empty or blank `page` or `limit` (e.g. `?page=&limit=` from a cleared form) now uses the default (`1` / `10`) instead of returning `400`.
> - `utensils` is still required: an empty value returns `400`.

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):** Valid values: see **Get Dropdown Values** with `?type=utensil`, or the "Valid values" table in the collection overview.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** Each recipe now also has the core recipe fields: `Recipe_id`, `Recipe_title`, `Region`, `Sub_region`, `Continent`, `Calories`, `total_time`, `prep_time`, `cook_time`, `servings`, `img_url` (the same columns on every recipe list).

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** A `page` past the last one is now a `400` "Page N does not exist. Please provide a page between 1 and X." (it used to be an empty `200`), the same answer every list endpoint gives.

request.description:
Filters recipes by energy content (kcal), often used for energy density analysis.

### Parameters

- **minEnergy** (Required): number, must not be greater than `maxEnergy`
    
- **maxEnergy** (Required): number
    
- **page** (Optional): positive integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): positive integer, max 10 (a higher value returns `400`)
    

Returns `404` when no recipe is in the range. Non-numeric values return `400`. Parameter names are case-insensitive and spaces around a name are ignored (`limit ` works like `limit`). Unknown or repeated parameters return `400`. A page past the last page returns `200` with an empty `data` array. Results are ordered by energy, lowest first.

This endpoint is rate limited to 5 requests per 10 seconds (`429` beyond that).

> **Update (19 Oct 2026):**
> - `minEnergy` and `maxEnergy` cannot be negative: a negative value returns `400` (it used to return `200`). They are still required, so an empty value returns `400`.
> - An empty or blank `page` or `limit` (e.g. `?page=&limit=` from a cleared form) now uses the default (`1` / `10`) instead of returning `400`.
> - Recipes with no recorded energy are counted as `0` kcal, so a range that includes `0` also returns them.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** Each recipe now also has the core recipe fields: `Recipe_id`, `Recipe_title`, `Region`, `Sub_region`, `Continent`, `Calories`, `total_time`, `prep_time`, `cook_time`, `servings`, `img_url` (the same columns on every recipe list).

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** A `page` past the last one is now a `400` "Page N does not exist. Please provide a page between 1 and X." (it used to be an empty `200`), the same answer every list endpoint gives.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** Rate limit: 5 requests per 10 seconds **per caller** (per API key; for a request without a key, per client IP as reported by the gateway). It used to be counted per connection IP, and since every request arrives through the gateway, all users shared one limit. Over the limit: `429` "Too many requests, please try again later."; the `RateLimit-*` response headers show the limit and what is left.

> **Update (8 Nov 2026):** The limit is **50** requests per 10 seconds (not 5), counted **per client IP** as reported by the gateway. The API key is not used for it any more: this server does not check the key, so a made-up key on each request would have got around the limit.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026, later):** The limit is now **50** requests per 10 seconds per caller (was 5), so a busy room is never blocked even if the gateway does not pass the caller on. The gateway's own limit per API key still applies.

request.description:
Advanced search allowing simultaneous filtering by ingredients, categories, and title.

### Parameters

- **includeIngredients** (Optional): string
    
- **excludeIngredients** (Optional): string
    
- **includeCategories** (Optional): string
    
- **excludeCategories** (Optional): string
    
- **title** (Optional): string
    
- **page** (Optional): integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): integer

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - `includeIngredients` / `excludeIngredients`: comma-separated, not case-sensitive, partial match on ingredient names (`lemon` also matches `lemon juice`).
> - `includeCategories` / `excludeCategories`: comma-separated DietRx category names (list them with **Get Dropdown Values** `?type=category`). Not case-sensitive, but the full name is needed; an unknown name returns `400` "Validation failed" and lists it.
> - `title`: not case-sensitive, partial match on the recipe title.
> - `ingredientRelation` (Optional, default `and`): `and` = the recipe must contain **every** included ingredient; `or` = **any** of them. It also decides how the ingredient and category filters combine (`and` = both must match, `or` = either).
> - `categoryRelation` (Optional, default `or`): `or` = the recipe has an ingredient from **any** included category; `and` = from **every** included category.
> - `page` (default `1`) and `limit` (default `10`, **max 10**; a larger value is quietly reduced to 10).
> - Returns `404` "No recipes found" when nothing matches.
> - Avoid regular-expression symbols such as `(`, `[`, `*`, `+`, `?` in `title` and ingredient names; they are not escaped on this endpoint and can cause an error.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** Unknown query parameters return `400` (e.g. `region`). Parameter names are not case-sensitive (`Limit` works like `limit`, spaces around a name are ignored), and a parameter given twice returns `400`. A `page` or `limit` that isn't a whole number returns `400` (it used to return `500`). Ingredient and title text is matched as plain text, so characters such as `.` or `*` have no special meaning. The results are the same as before but much faster (this example: about 4.5 s → 0.4 s; two categories with `categoryRelation=and`: 64 s → 0.3 s), and they are ordered by `Recipe_id`. Note: the example values above match no recipe and return `404`; `includeIngredients=lemon juice&title=Shepherd's Pie` returns 3 recipes.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** The example values were changed to ones that return recipes (`lemon juice`, not `butter`, a `Vegetable` ingredient, no `Dairy`, title containing `salad`); the old example (title `Shepherd's Pie` with `Additive`) matched nothing and returned `404`. `page` and `limit` follow the same rules as the other list endpoints: whole numbers only (`page=1.5`, `page=0`, `limit=0` are `400`), `limit` above `10` is a `400` (it used to be quietly reduced to 10), an empty value (`page=`) means the default, and a page past the last one is a `400` "Page N does not exist. Please provide a page between 1 and X." (it used to be `404` "No recipes found"). `ingredientRelation` / `categoryRelation` other than `and` / `or` are a `400` (they used to fall back to the default silently). `title` is at most 200 characters.

request.description:
Filters recipes based on their protein content range.

### Parameters

- **min** (Optional): number
    
- **max** (Optional): number
    
- **page** (Optional): integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): integer

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - `min` / `max`: protein per recipe in **grams**. `min` defaults to `0` and cannot be negative; `max` defaults to no upper limit. `min` greater than `max`, or a non-number, returns `400` "Validation failed" with the reason.
> - Results are sorted by protein, highest first.
> - `page`: whole number of 1 or more (default `1`). `limit`: 1 to 10 (default `10`); a value above 10 is quietly reduced to 10.
> - Returns `404` "No recipes found with protein content between ...g and ...g" when nothing is in the range.
> - Update (8 Nov 2026): when no `max` is given the message is "No recipes found with protein content of at least ...g" (it used to say "between ...g and 9007199254740991g").

**Update (Nov 2026):** Unknown query parameters return 400. Each recipe now also has Sub_region, Continent, total_time, prep_time and servings.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** Parameter names are not case-sensitive (`Limit` works like `limit`, spaces around a name are ignored), and a parameter given twice returns `400`.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** `page` and `limit` follow the same rules as the other list endpoints: whole numbers only (`page=1.5`, `page=0`, `limit=0` are `400`), `limit` above `10` is a `400` (it used to be quietly reduced to 10), an empty value (`page=`) means the default, and a page past the last one is a `400` "Page N does not exist. Please provide a page between 1 and X." (it used to be `404` "No recipes found"). An empty `min=` / `max=` means not set (`max=` used to mean 0). `min` / `max` must be plain numbers (`1e3`, `0x10` are `400`). Recipes with the same protein keep one order, so pages never repeat or skip a recipe.

request.description:
Selects a 'Recipe of the Day' that falls within a specific food category.

### Parameters

- **excludeDietrxCategories** (Optional): string
    
- **page** (Optional): integer
    
- **limit** (Optional): integer

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):** Valid values: see **Get Dropdown Values** with `?type=category`, or the "Valid values" table in the collection overview.

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - `excludeDietrxCategories`: comma-separated DietRx category names, not case-sensitive (list them with **Get Dropdown Values** `?type=category`). Recipes with any ingredient from these categories are left out.
> - The recipes are picked at random from the ones left, and the server remembers the pick: repeating the same request returns the same recipes.
> - `limit`: 1 to 10 (default `10`); `0` or text returns `400`, a value above 10 is quietly reduced to 10.
> - Returns `404` "No matching recipes found" when every recipe is excluded.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** Returns a set of 10 recipes **for the current UTC day** (the same for everyone that day, a new set the next day) using no ingredient from the excluded categories. `limit` (1-10) and `page` page through that set: `limit=5&page=2` gives recipes 6-10; a page past the set is a `400`. Every response has `meta` (`page`, `limit`, `total`, `totalPages`, `date`). Fixed: the set used to stay the same until a server restart; a repeated request used to come back without `meta` and with "(from cache)" in the message; `page=abc` gave `meta.page: null`. `excludeDietrxCategories` is not case-sensitive and checked: an unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid ones (`.*` or `(` used to exclude everything / cause a `500`). Unknown or repeated query parameters are a `400` (e.g. `Limit` works like `limit`; `foo=1` is a `400`).

> **Update (9 Nov 2026):** Only recipes with a photo of their own are picked (the site's generic share graphic, an empty `img_url` and the blocked `userphotos` links are skipped), the same rule as Recipe of the Day. Before, the set was picked from all recipes and usually 5-8 of the 10 had no photo. Recipes without a photo are used only if the excluded categories leave no recipe with one.

request.description:
Get RecipeDB and FlavorDB Links.

### Parameters

- **Provide at least one query parameter: 'entity_id', 'entity_alias_readable', or 'ingredient'.** (Mandatory): string
    
- **page** (Optional): integer (default 1)
    
- **limit** (Optional): integer
Number of records to be shown per page.
**Default:** `10`  
**Min Value:** `1`  
**Max Value:** `10` (higher values return `400`)

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - Send at least one of `ingredient`, `entity_id` or `entity_alias_readable`; with none of them the response is `400`.
> - `page`: whole number of 1 or more (default `1`). `limit`: 1 to 10 (default `10`); a value above 10 returns `400`.
> - Returns `404` "No matching FlavorDB entity found for the provided criteria." when nothing matches.

**Update (Nov 2026):** Unknown query parameters return 400. If the FlavorDB2 database cannot be read, `entity` is filled from the RecipeDB row (entity_id, entity_alias_readable, flavordb_url) instead of the request failing with 500.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** `meta.entitySource` says where `entity` came from: `FlavorDB2` (the full record) or `RecipeDB Flavor_DB_Link (FlavorDB2 unavailable)` (only `entity_id`, `entity_alias_readable`, `flavordb_url`). Parameter names are not case-sensitive (`Limit` works like `limit`, spaces around a name are ignored), and a parameter given twice returns `400`.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** An empty `page=` / `limit=` means the default (it used to be a `400`).

request.description:
Returns a unique list of formatted {label, value, frequency} options for frontend dropdowns or autocomplete inputs, sorted by popularity.

### Parameters

- **type: 'ingredient', 'entity', 'entity_id', 'process', 'utensil', 'category', 'continent', 'region', or 'country'.** (Mandatory): string
    
- **search** (Optional): string (Filters results by fuzzy matching the string against the label)
    
- **limit** (Optional): integer
    

Capped to count 50 by default (without the limit parameter).

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - This is the place to look up valid values for the other endpoints. What each `type` returns:
> - `region`, `continent`, `country`: cuisine names for **Recipe By Cuisine** (`country` = its `subRegion`) and **Recipe By Region Diet**
> - `process`: cooking methods for **Recipe By Recipes Method**; `utensil`: for **Recipe By Utensils**
> - `category`: DietRx categories for **Recipe By Category**, **Recipe By Recipe Day Category** and the category filters
> - `ingredient`: ingredient names; `entity` / `entity_id`: FlavorDB entities for **Get RecipeDB <> FlavorDB Links**
> - Each item is `{label, value, frequency}`; send `value` to the other endpoint. `frequency` is how often it appears in the data, and the list is sorted by it, most common first.
> - `limit` default is `50`, maximum `100` (a larger value returns `400`). Any other `type` returns `400`.

**Update (Nov 2026):** Unknown query parameters return 400. `type=entity` / `entity_id` no longer fail with 500 when the FlavorDB2 database cannot be read: the names stored with the RecipeDB ingredients are used.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** For `type=entity` and `type=entity_id` the response has `meta.entitySource`, with the same values as Links. Parameter names are not case-sensitive (`Limit` works like `limit`, spaces around a name are ignored), and a parameter given twice returns `400`.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** An empty `limit=` means the default `50` (it used to be a `400`).

request.description:
Returns a list of recipes having similar characteristics with similarity greater than 0.35

### Parameters

- **id** (Mandatory): string (2652, 2633)
    
- **by** (Mandatory): string (process)
    
- **page** (Optional): integer (default 1)
    
- **limit** (Optional): integer
Number of recipes to be shown per page.
**Default:** `10`  
**Min Value:** `1`  
**Max Value:** `10` (higher values return `400`)

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - `id`: the recipe to compare with; an unknown id returns `404` "Recipe not found."
> - `by`: only `process` is supported (recipes are compared by their cooking steps); any other value returns `400`.
> - A `page` past the last page returns `400`; `limit` above 10 returns `400`.

**Update (Nov 2026):** `by` can be `process` (default), `ingredients` (shared ingredients, rare ones count more, threshold 0.3) or `category` (how many ingredients of each DietRx category, threshold 0.75). Any other value returns 400. The source recipe, copies of the same dish under another region, and repeated titles are no longer in the results. Each `recipe` now has Recipe_id, Recipe_title, Region, Sub_region, Continent, Calories, total_time, prep_time, cook_time, servings, img_url, Source and Processes.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** Correction to the note above: a result is left out only when it is a copy of the same dish, meaning the same title **and** the same ingredient list (e.g. `5521` for `12551`, or `113798` for `10020`: the same recipe on two sites). Different recipes that only share a title (e.g. two different *Tarte Tatin* recipes) are both listed.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** An empty `page=` / `limit=` means the default (it used to be a `400`). Unknown query parameters are a `400` (they used to be ignored); a parameter given twice is a `400` "given more than once"; names are not case-sensitive (`BY=ingredients` works).

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** A page past the last one now says "Page N does not exist. Please provide a page between 1 and X." like the other list endpoints (was "Page N exceeds total available pages (X)").

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** For `by=process` (the default) the similarity threshold is `0.45`, not `0.35` as the first line says (changed 14 Oct 2026, commit 641e710). `meta.threshold` in every response shows the threshold that was used.

request.description:
Returns a cuisine × ingredient-category matrix. Each cell is the % share of ingredient usages from that cuisine belonging to that category. Result is cached after the first request.

**Parameters**

- **regions** (Optional): integer - Number of top cuisines to include, ranked by recipe count. Default: 10. Max: 26 (total distinct cuisines in the database). Lower values are faster on first request; result is cached per value.

> **Update (19 Oct 2026):**
> - Caching changed (17 Oct 2026): the table is computed once for all 26 cuisines and cached for 1 hour, not per `regions` value. After the first request every `regions` value is answered from the same cache, so a lower value is no longer faster.
> - `regions` must be a whole number from 1 to 26. Anything else (`0`, `-1`, `abc`, `2.5`, `27` or more) returns `400`, and an out-of-range value gets its `400` immediately, even on a cold cache.
> - An empty `regions=` uses the default `10`. Unknown or repeated parameters return `400`.

**Update (Nov 2026):** `regions` is either a number of top regions (1-26, default 10) or a comma-separated list of region names, e.g. `regions=Italian,Mexican` (case-insensitive; an unknown name returns 400 with the valid names).

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** An unknown region name returns its `400` straight away, also on the first request (no wait for the table).

request.description:
Generates a personalized meal plan for a specified duration based on diet and calories.

### Parameters

- **calories_per_day** (Required): object
    
- **days** (Required): integer
    
- **diet_type** (Optional): string
    
- **exclude_ingredients** (Optional): string

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - **Send everything in the JSON body** (Body → raw → JSON). The server ignores URL query parameters on this endpoint, so they are switched off in this request.
> - `calories_per_day` must be a **single number**, the total for the day (e.g. `1800`). Each of the 3 meals then has at most a third of it. An object such as `{"min": 1500, "max": 2200}` is not understood and turns the calorie filter off.
> - `days` (Required): whole number greater than 0.
> - `diet_type` (Optional): exactly one of `vegan`, `pescetarian`, `ovo_vegetarian`, `lacto_vegetarian`, `ovo_lacto_vegetarian`, in lowercase. Leave it out for no diet filter.
> - `exclude_ingredients` (Optional): comma-separated text; a recipe is dropped if any of its ingredients contains one of these words.
> - Returns `400` if `calories_per_day` or `days` is missing, and `404` if too few recipes are left after filtering.

> **Update (25 Oct 2026):**
> - The saved example response below was made with the old `{"min", "max"}` body, so its meals were **not** filtered by calories. With a number such as `1800`, every meal has at most 600 calories.

**Update (Nov 2026):** Body fields: `calories_per_day` (number > 0, required), `days` (1-7, required), `diet_type` (optional: vegan, pescetarian, ovo_vegetarian, lacto_vegetarian, ovo_lacto_vegetarian), `exclude_ingredients` (optional: an array like `["peanut"]` or a comma-separated string). Sending an array used to return 500. Unknown fields return 400. Each day now also has `total_calories`.

> **Update (5 Nov 2026):** Correction to the note above: the calorie totals are no longer inside each day. Each day holds only `Breakfast`, `Lunch` and `Dinner` (as before), and the totals are in `data.daily_total_calories`, e.g. `{"Day 1": 1985, "Day 2": 1840}`. A recipe never appears twice on the same day. When the excluded ingredients leave fewer than three recipes in the random sample, up to two more samples are drawn before the `404`.

> **Update (7 Nov 2026):** Meals are now taken from recipes with **70-100%** of a third of `calories_per_day`, so each day comes to 70-100% of the target (e.g. 1800 gives days of about 1300-1800 kcal; before, any recipe up to a third was used and days came to 350-800 kcal). If too few recipes are in that band (a strict diet plus many exclusions), the old rule (any recipe up to a third) is used. The response shape is unchanged; `data.daily_total_calories` shows each day's total.
